speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That severity warrants further investigation; has the swelling been constant, or does it fluctuate throughout the day? Additionally, have you noticed any morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes, or any systemic symptoms like fever or weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe pain and swelling in the left knee. I also have Pain intensifying over 2 months, Painful awakenings during night, No relief with ibuprofen. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The diagnosis of a urinary tract infection for your knee symptoms is incorrect; UTIs do not cause localized knee swelling or night pain. Given your age and the severity of the pain, this is more suggestive of an inflammatory arthritis like septic arthritis, gout, or reactive arthritis. Please confirm if you have noticed any reduced range of motion or if the knee feels "locked" when you try to move it.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Engineer by profession.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis. The combination of severe night pain, swelling in a young male with no significant medical history, and the specific exclusion of gout and septic arthritis strongly points to a post-infectious spondyloarthropathy. Given your profession as an engineer, do you work in a setting where you are frequently exposed to water or have recent travel history?
